key_insight: A multi-modal temporal attention model using welding images and sound can detect hard-to-see fillet-joint defects in real time with near-perfect accuracy and explainable outputs.
engineering_relevance: This enables earlier, more reliable in-process quality control for gas metal arc welding, reducing rework, delays, and undetected internal defects.
method: Trained a deep learning defect detector on synchronized welding image and audio data from an industrial collaborative robot.
Used temporal attention to focus on the most informative moments during welding.
Applied explainable AI to identify influential regions in images and spectrograms and to compare modality usefulness across defect types.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the attention module improved the F1 score to 0.99 on defect detection and that the model was evaluated on collected real welding images and sound data.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the specific sensor setup and weld conditions, so deployment will require careful calibration and validation across different joints and production environments.
paper_title: Explainable Temporal Attention-based Defect Detection For Fillet Joints in Real-Time Gas Metal Arc Welding Based on Multi-modal Data
